newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity's Magellan cut stock holdings in November.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity's Magellan cut stock holdings in November.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Monday its Magellan Fund cut its holdings in equities to 88.5 percent of total assets at the end of November from 89.8 percent a month earlier.
According to Fidelity's monthly mutual fund guide, the massive fund raised its holdings in cash and other securities to 3.6 percent from 1.5 percent.
Assets invested in bonds continued to dwindle, dropping to 7.9 percent from 8.7 percent.
Magellan raised its investments in technology stocks to 13.6 percent from 11.6 percent, the guide said.
Shares in energy companies remained Magellan's top sectorial holding, but manager Robert Stansky trimmed the energy holdings to 13.9 percent from 14.0 percent.
Stansky added Philip Morris Cos Inc to the fund's top 10 holdings and cut Conrail Inc from the list. The rest of the top 10 remained unchanged.
U.S. Treasury notes maturing in 2005 remained at the top of Magellan's top 10 holdings, followed by Intel Corp, General Electric Co and Chrysler Corp.
Magellan's assets fell to $53.988 billion at the end of December from $55.851 billion at the end of November.
Magellan's investments in foreign assets fell to 10.6 percent at the end of November from 11.6 percent at the end of October, the fund guide said.
Magellan recorded a total return for 1996, excluding a three percent sales charge, of 11.69 percent, against 22.96 percent for the S&P500, the fund guide said.

Also among sectorial holdings, Magellan's investments in durables fell to 10.1 percent from 10.3 percent, in finance shares rose to 8.7 percent from 8.6 percent, and in industrial machinery and equipment slipped to 8.2 percent from 8.4 percent.
Magellan's holdings in health care companies rose to 3.6 percent from 3.3 percent.
